18:1.sourceText: Μετὰ ταῦτα χωρισθεὶς ἐκ τῶν Ἀθηνῶν ἦλθεν εἰς Κόρινθον.
18:1.targetText: And after these things, Paul having departed out of Athens, came to Corinth,

groups.note: Actual χωρισθείς is an aorist passive participle, having separated or departed, rendered having departed; its actual passive-form analysis is retained.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with Athens has no separate English counterpart.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR has an additional δέ connective near the start; it is absent from the pinned N1904 verse.
The checked TR explicitly names Paul here; the pinned N1904 has no written Paul name in this verse.

18:2.sourceText: καὶ εὑρών τινα Ἰουδαῖον ὀνόματι Ἀκύλαν, Ποντικὸν τῷ γένει, προσφάτως ἐληλυθότα ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰταλίας καὶ Πρίσκιλλαν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, διὰ τὸ διατεταχέναι Κλαύδιον χωρίζεσθαι πάντας τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ἀπὸ τῆς Ῥώμης, προσῆλθεν αὐτοῖς,
18:2.targetText: and having found a certain Jew, by name Aquilas, of Pontus by birth, lately come from Italy, and his wife Priscilla—because of Claudius having directed all the Jews to depart out of Rome—he came to them,

groups.note: Actual Ποντικόν is an ethnic adjective, recorded A-ASM, rendered of Pontus. It does not supply an independently written place-name noun plus preposition.
The actual dative article and birth or family noun jointly supply by birth; no separate Greek by preposition is printed.

Actual διά with the accusative article introduces the causal articular-infinitive clause, rendered because of. The real directing infinitive and its accusative Claudius subject retain their own source identities.

Actual χωρίζεσθαι has functional passive V-PPN and form V-PEN analyses, rendered to depart. Both tags describe the same printed infinitive; English does not supply a separate source verb for departure.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with Italy and Rome have no separate English counterparts.

18:3.sourceText: καὶ διὰ τὸ ὁμότεχνον εἶναι ἔμενεν παρ’ αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἠργάζοντο· ἦσαν γὰρ σκηνοποιοὶ τῇ τέχνῃ.
18:3.targetText: and because of being of the same craft, he remained with them, and was working, for they were tentmakers as to craft;

groups.note: Actual ὁμότεχνον is one same-trade adjective, rendered of the same craft; separate of, same, and craft source words are not invented.

Actual ἠργάζοντο is imperfect middle third-person plural, they were working; the checked TR has singular ἠργάζετο behind was working. The working predicate stays linked while the actual source number remains explicit.

The actual dative article and craft noun jointly supply as to craft, a respect relation. The checked TR instead has an accusative craft expression; neither source is retagged from the English wording.

18:4.sourceText: διελέγετο δὲ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον, ἔπειθέν τε Ἰουδαίους καὶ Ἕλληνας.
18:4.targetText: and he was reasoning in the synagogue every Sabbath, persuading both Jews and Greeks.

groups.note: Actual κατά with every forms the distributive every-Sabbath expression; both source words remain one distributive constituent.
Actual ἔπειθεν is imperfect active indicative third-person singular; English uses the participial wording persuading for that actual finite persuasion predicate.

18:5.sourceText: Ὡς δὲ κατῆλθον ἀπὸ τῆς Μακεδονίας ὅ τε Σιλᾶς καὶ ὁ Τιμόθεος, συνείχετο τῷ λόγῳ ὁ Παῦλος, διαμαρτυρόμενος τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις εἶναι τὸν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν.
18:5.targetText: And when both Silas and Timotheus came down from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in the Spirit, testifying fully to the Jews Jesus the Christ;

groups.note: Actual συνείχετο has functional passive V-IPI-3S and form V-IEI-3S analyses, rendered was pressed; these describe one printed source form.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with Macedonia and the three personal names have no separate English counterparts.
Actual τῷ λόγῳ is the dative word expression, while the checked TR writes τῷ πνεύματι behind English in the Spirit. The unlike nominal heads are kept explicitly unpaired.
N1904 writes the being infinitive εἶναι in the testimony content; the checked TR omits it and English juxtaposes Jesus and the Christ without a separate being word.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR has the Spirit expression here, whereas N1904 has the word expression.

18:6.sourceText: ἀντιτασσομένων δὲ αὐτῶν καὶ βλασφημούντων ἐκτιναξάμενος τὰ ἱμάτια εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Τὸ αἷμα ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν ὑμῶν· καθαρὸς ἐγώ· ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν εἰς τὰ ἔθνη πορεύσομαι.
18:6.targetText: and on their resisting and slandering, having shaken [his] garments, he said to them, “Your blood [is] on your head—I am clean; from now on I will go on to the nations.”

groups.note: The actual genitive resisting participle and personal genitive form the circumstance clause; English on expresses that relation without an independently printed Greek on preposition.

Actual definite article and garments noun identify the immediately acting subject’s clothing under the middle shaking predicate. English bracketed his expresses that subject-related definite clothing construction. No independently printed possessive or autos pronoun is claimed.
Actual article plus now forms the temporal from-now expression; English now on renders this whole temporal construction after from, not an independent source on word.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with your blood and your head have no separate English counterparts beside the possessives.

unmappedTarget.reason: This bracketed English copula has no independently written Greek being word in the blood-on-your-head clause.
The English copula in I am clean is supplied for the nominal adjective clause; no Greek being word is written there.

18:7.sourceText: καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ἦλθεν εἰς οἰκίαν τινὸς ὀνόματι Τιτίου Ἰούστου σεβομένου τὸν Θεόν, οὗ ἡ οἰκία ἦν συνομοροῦσα τῇ συναγωγῇ.
18:7.targetText: And having departed from there, he went to the house of a certain one, by name Justus, a worshiper of God, whose house was adjoining the synagogue,

groups.note: Actual σεβομένου is a substantival worshiping participle, rendered a worshiper; no independently printed worshiper noun is invented.
Actual accusative article and God noun are the object of worshiping; English nominal worshiper recasts this relation as of God. The original accusative analysis is retained, not changed to genitive.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 additionally names Titius before Justus; the checked TR and this English verse have no Titius counterpart.
The Greek article with whose house has no separate English counterpart beside whose.

18:8.sourceText: Κρίσπος δὲ ὁ ἀρχισυνάγωγος ἐπίστευσεν τῷ Κυρίῳ σὺν ὅλῳ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ, καὶ πολλοὶ τῶν Κορινθίων ἀκούοντες ἐπίστευον καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο.
18:8.targetText: and Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue believed in the LORD with all his house, and many of the Corinthians hearing were believing, and they were being immersed.

groups.note: Actual ἀρχισυνάγωγος is one synagogue-ruler compound noun, rendered ruler of the synagogue; no independent source ruler and synagogue nouns are printed.
The actual dative article and Lord noun supply the belief complement in the LORD; no independent Greek in preposition is written.
Actual ἐβαπτίζοντο is imperfect passive functionally, V-IPI-3P, with form V-IEI-3P, rendered they were being immersed. Both analyses belong to one real source verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with all his house has no separate English counterpart beside the possessive.

18:9.sourceText: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Κύριος ἐν νυκτὶ δι’ ὁράματος τῷ Παύλῳ Μὴ φοβοῦ, ἀλλὰ λάλει καὶ μὴ σιωπήσῃς,
18:9.targetText: And the LORD said through a vision in the night to Paul, “Do not be afraid, but be speaking and you may not be silent;

groups.note: Actual dative article and Paul name jointly identify the addressed recipient, rendered to Paul without an independent Greek to preposition.

Actual σιωπήσῃς is aorist active subjunctive second-person singular under prohibitive μή, rendered you may not be silent. It is not assigned an indicative or imperative tag from the English auxiliary wording.

18:10.sourceText: διότι ἐγώ εἰμι μετὰ σοῦ καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπιθήσεταί σοι τοῦ κακῶσαί σε, διότι λαός ἐστί μοι πολὺς ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ.
18:10.targetText: because I am with you, and no one will set on you to do evil [to] you, because I have many people in this city”;

groups.note: Actual genitive article and harming infinitive form the purpose construction to do evil. The actual articular infinitive stays together; no bare English to is isolated on the article.
Actual σε is the accusative person harmed; English do evil recasts that same affected person as bracketed to you. The source remains accusative, without an invented Greek to preposition.

Actual ἐστί μοι is a being-plus-dative possession construction, people are to me, rendered I have people. The real copula and dative first-person pronoun jointly supply I have; there is no printed ἔχω verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with this city has no separate English counterpart beside this.

18:11.sourceText: Ἐκάθισεν δὲ ἐνιαυτὸν καὶ μῆνας ἓξ διδάσκων ἐν αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ.
18:11.targetText: and he continued a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.

groups.note: Actual ἐκάθισεν is the aorist active sat or stayed predicate, rendered he continued. Its actual καθίζω identity is retained rather than substituting a different continuing verb.

18:12.sourceText: Γαλλίωνος δὲ ἀνθυπάτου ὄντος τῆς Ἀχαΐας κατεπέστησαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ βῆμα,
18:12.targetText: And Gallio being proconsul of Achaia, the Jews made a rush with one accord on Paul, and brought him to the judgment seat,

groups.note: Actual ἀνθυπάτου is a genitive proconsul noun with the real being participle; the checked TR instead uses the related proconsul-serving participle. The actual noun and being word retain distinct identities.
Actual genitive article and Achaia name jointly supply of Achaia; the relation is not detached from its real nominal head.
Actual dative article and Paul name express the person rushed upon under the attack predicate, rendered on Paul; no extra source on preposition is invented.

18:13.sourceText: λέγοντες ὅτι Παρὰ τὸν νόμον ἀναπείθει οὗτος τοὺς ἀνθρώπους σέβεσθαι τὸν Θεόν.
18:13.targetText: saying, “This one persuades men to worship God against the Law”;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek report particle is expressed by English direct quotation without a separate that.
The Greek articles with men and God have no separate English counterparts.

18:14.sourceText: μέλλοντος δὲ τοῦ Παύλου ἀνοίγειν τὸ στόμα εἶπεν ὁ Γαλλίων πρὸς τοὺς Ἰουδαίους Εἰ μὲν ἦν ἀδίκημά τι ἢ ῥᾳδιούργημα πονηρόν, ὦ Ἰουδαῖοι, κατὰ λόγον ἂν ἀνεσχόμην ὑμῶν·
18:14.targetText: and Paul being about to open [his] mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If, indeed, then, it was anything unrighteous, or an act of wicked recklessness, O Jews, according to reason I had borne with you,

groups.note: The actual definite article and mouth noun identify the opening subject’s own body part, rendered bracketed his mouth. No independently written possessive pronoun is claimed.
Actual ἀδίκημα is an unrighteous deed noun, rendered adjectivally as unrighteous after anything. Its recorded N-NSN noun analysis is retained rather than replaced by an adjective tag.
Actual ῥᾳδιούργημα is one reckless-act noun; English expands it as an act of ... recklessness with wicked retaining its own adjective anchor.

Actual potential ἄν and aorist middle indicative ἀνεσχόμην form the conditional bearing-with predicate, rendered I had borne with. The particle is retained with its actual verbal head, not an invented separate English would word.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with Paul and Gallio have no separate English counterparts.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR has an additional οὖν after indeed; N1904 has no corresponding then connective here.

18:15.sourceText: εἰ δὲ ζητήματά ἐστιν περὶ λόγου καὶ ὀνομάτων καὶ νόμου τοῦ καθ’ ὑμᾶς, ὄψεσθε αὐτοί· κριτὴς ἐγὼ τούτων οὐ βούλομαι εἶναι.
18:15.targetText: but if it is a question concerning words and names, and of your law, look [to it] yourselves, for I do not intend to be a judge of these things,”

groups.note: Actual ζητήματα is a plural question or dispute noun; the checked TR instead has singular ζήτημα behind English a question. The same question head is retained with its actual plural analysis.

Actual λόγου is singular word, while English renders words in this coordinated subject matter; the checked TR also has singular λόγου. This is a rendering number difference, not a claimed difference between the two printed witnesses.
Actual νόμου is genitive law, rendered of ... law with your separately anchored. The relational of stays with the actual nominal head.
Actual καθ᾽ ὑμᾶς specifies the law among you; English recasts that association as possessive your. The actual pronoun is accusative, not an independently written genitive possessive.
Actual ὄψεσθε is future second-person plural, recorded V-FDI-2P, rendered directive look. The original future form is retained rather than retagged imperative.
Actual αὐτοί is nominative plural intensive, you yourselves, rendered yourselves. It is not an independently written reflexive pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article qualifies the law as the one among you; English your law has no separately expressed article.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR has an additional γάρ before I do not intend; the pinned N1904 has no corresponding for connective at that point.
English supplies this bracketed attention object under look; neither the pinned N1904 nor the checked TR writes a separate personal or demonstrative object at that verb.

18:16.sourceText: καὶ ἀπήλασεν αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ βήματος.
18:16.targetText: and he drives them from the judgment seat;

groups.note: Actual ἀπήλασεν is aorist active indicative third-person singular; English narrates the same driving-away action with present he drives.

18:17.sourceText: ἐπιλαβόμενοι δὲ πάντες Σωσθένην τὸν ἀρχισυνάγωγον ἔτυπτον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ βήματος· καὶ οὐδὲν τούτων τῷ Γαλλίωνι ἔμελεν.
18:17.targetText: and all the Greeks having taken Sosthenes, the chief man of the synagogue, were beating [him] before the judgment seat, and Gallio was not even caring for these things.

groups.note: The one actual Sosthenes name is the immediately taken and beaten patient. English repeats him after beating; no additional original pronoun is invented.

Actual ἀρχισυνάγωγον is one synagogue-chief compound noun, rendered chief man of the synagogue. The additional English man and synagogue words are components of the one title rendering, not separately printed source nouns.

Actual ἔμελεν is the imperfect impersonal care predicate, with the concern as subject and Gallio as dative experiencer. English recasts this as Gallio was not even caring; the original impersonal construction is retained in the source analyses.
Actual οὐδέν is the nominative negative indefinite nothing, not a separately printed adverb; English recasts its negation as not even in the caring clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with Gallio has no separate English counterpart.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR names the Greeks here, while N1904 writes only all without the article and Greek-people noun.

18:18.sourceText: Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔτι προσμείνας ἡμέρας ἱκανὰς, τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ἀποταξάμενος ἐξέπλει εἰς τὴν Συρίαν, καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ Πρίσκιλλα καὶ Ἀκύλας, κειράμενος ἐν Κενχρεαῖς τὴν κεφαλήν· εἶχεν γὰρ εὐχήν.
18:18.targetText: And Paul having remained yet a good many days, having taken leave of the brothers, was sailing to Syria—and with him [are] Priscilla and Aquilas—having shorn [his] head in Cenchera, for he had a vow;

groups.note: Actual dative article and brothers noun express the leave-taking recipients; English nominal leave recasts that relation as of the brothers. The original case remains dative, not genitive.

The actual definite article and head noun express the middle haircutting participant’s own body part, rendered bracketed his head. This does not add a printed possessive pronoun or assign the shaving action to a separately invented named subject.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with Paul and Syria have no separate English counterparts.

unmappedTarget.reason: The bracketed copula before the companions is supplied in English; neither N1904 nor the checked TR writes a being word there.

18:19.sourceText: κατήντησαν δὲ εἰς Ἔφεσον, κἀκείνους κατέλιπεν αὐτοῦ, αὐτὸς δὲ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν διελέξατο τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις.
18:19.targetText: and he came down to Ephesus, and left them there, and he himself having entered into the synagogue reasoned with the Jews:

groups.note: Actual κατήντησαν is aorist active indicative third-person plural, they arrived; checked TR has singular κατήντησεν behind he came down. The actual arrival head remains linked without changing its recorded number.
Actual κἀκείνους is the crasis of and with those people; English splits the same one source form as and ... them.
Actual αὐτοῦ is recorded ADV in both analyses and means there; it is not a personal genitive pronoun at this occurrence.
Actual αὐτός is nominative singular intensive, rendered he himself. The source is not independently tagged as a reflexive pronoun.
Actual dative article and Jews expression supply the reasoning partners, rendered with the Jews. No separate Greek with preposition is written there.

18:20.sourceText: ἐρωτώντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐπὶ πλείονα χρόνον μεῖναι οὐκ ἐπένευσεν,
18:20.targetText: and they having requested [him] to remain a longer time with them, he did not consent,

groups.note: Actual αὐτῶν is the genitive plural subject of the requesting participle in the genitive absolute; English recasts the same people as nominative they. The actual genitive pronoun is retained.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual ἐπί marks the extended time expression; English a longer time has no separately expressed duration preposition.

unmappedTarget.reason: The request recipient is supplied in this English verse; neither N1904 nor the checked TR writes an independent object pronoun after requesting.
The checked TR writes the additional παρ᾽ αὐτοῖς phrase; it is absent from the pinned N1904 verse.

18:21.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ἀποταξάμενος καὶ εἰπών Πάλιν ἀνακάμψω πρὸς ὑμᾶς τοῦ Θεοῦ θέλοντος, ἀνήχθη ἀπὸ τῆς Ἐφέσου,
18:21.targetText: but took leave of them, saying, “It is necessary for me by all means to keep the coming celebration at Jerusalem, and again I will return to you—God willing.” And he sailed from Ephesus,

groups.note: Actual ἀποταξάμενος is an aorist middle participle; English recasts the leave-taking predicate as took leave of. The actual source remains participial, not finite.
Actual ἀνήχθη is aorist passive, was put out to sea, rendered he sailed. The source passive form is retained rather than replaced by an active sailing verb.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 writes καί joining the leave-taking and saying participles; English has no and at that construction. The TR coordination before sailing is a different location and is not substituted for this source occurrence.
The Greek articles with God and Ephesus have no separate English counterparts.

unmappedTarget.reason: Checked TR has an additional αὐτοῖς leave-taking recipient; N1904 does not write that personal recipient here.

unmappedTarget.text: It is necessary for me by all means to keep the coming celebration at Jerusalem
unmappedTarget.reason: This entire celebration-in-Jerusalem clause is present in the checked TR and this English wording but absent from the pinned N1904 verse; no source identities are borrowed from another verse.
This connective before again follows checked TR δέ; N1904 starts the quoted return promise with again and no such connective.
The checked TR writes καί before sailed; N1904 has no connective at that clause boundary.

18:22.sourceText: καὶ κατελθὼν εἰς Καισάριαν, ἀναβὰς καὶ ἀσπασάμενος τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, κατέβη εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν,
18:22.targetText: and having come down to Caesarea, having gone up, and having greeted the assembly, he went down to Antioch.

18:23.sourceText: καὶ ποιήσας χρόνον τινὰ ἐξῆλθεν, διερχόμενος καθεξῆς τὴν Γαλατικὴν χώραν καὶ Φρυγίαν, στηρίζων πάντας τοὺς μαθητάς.
18:23.targetText: And having stayed some time, he went forth, going successively through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.

groups.note: Actual ποιήσας with time is the spending-time idiom, rendered having stayed some time. The original is ποιέω in this temporal use, not a separately written staying verb.
Actual Γαλατικήν is a territorial adjective, recorded A-ASF, rendered of Galatia. No independent Galatia place-name noun or of preposition is invented.
Actual στηρίζων is from στηρίζω, strengthening; checked TR has the related prefixed ἐπιστηρίζων. The actual unprefixed source head is retained.

18:24.sourceText: Ἰουδαῖος δέ τις Ἀπολλῶς ὀνόματι, Ἀλεξανδρεὺς τῷ γένει, ἀνὴρ λόγιος, κατήντησεν εἰς Ἔφεσον, δυνατὸς ὢν ἐν ταῖς γραφαῖς.
18:24.targetText: And a certain Jew, Apollos by name, an Alexandrian by birth, a man of eloquence, being mighty in the Writings, came to Ephesus;

groups.note: Actual Ἀλεξανδρεύς is an ethnic noun, recorded N-NSM in both analyses, rendered an Alexandrian. The recorded noun analysis is retained.
The actual dative article and birth or family noun jointly supply by birth; the English by is not an independently written Greek preposition.
Actual λόγιος is an eloquent or learned adjective, rendered of eloquence as a nominal modifier. No separate Greek eloquence noun is invented.

18:25.sourceText: οὗτος ἦν κατηχημένος τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ Κυρίου, καὶ ζέων τῷ πνεύματι ἐλάλει καὶ ἐδίδασκεν ἀκριβῶς τὰ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ἐπιστάμενος μόνον τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάνου·
18:25.targetText: this one was instructed in the way of the LORD, and being fervent in the Spirit, was speaking and teaching exactly the things about the LORD, knowing only the immersion of John;

groups.note: Actual κατηχημένος is a perfect passive participle with the written imperfect copula, forming the instructed periphrasis. English was instructed retains those real source words without changing the participle to an aorist.

Actual accusative article and way noun express the content of instruction; English uses in the way. Both real case-bearing nominal words stay together, without a separately printed Greek in preposition.
Actual ζέων is a present active boiling or fervent participle, rendered being fervent. Its English being belongs to this real verbal participle, not an invented separate Greek copula.
The actual dative article and spirit noun jointly supply in the Spirit. This records the case construction without inventing a separate Greek in preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article and Jesus name differ from the checked TR article and LORD title followed by this English second the LORD. The unlike named heads remain explicit witness gaps.

unmappedTarget.reason: The second LORD expression follows checked TR τοῦ κυρίου; N1904 instead has τοῦ Ἰησοῦ at this occurrence.

18:26.sourceText: οὗτός τε ἤρξατο παρρησιάζεσθαι ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ. ἀκούσαντες δὲ αὐτοῦ Πρίσκιλλα καὶ Ἀκύλας προσελάβοντο αὐτὸν καὶ ἀκριβέστερον αὐτῷ ἐξέθεντο τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ.
18:26.targetText: this one also began to speak boldly in the synagogue, and Aquilas and Priscilla having heard of him, took him to [them], and more exactly set forth to him The Way of God,

groups.note: Actual αὐτοῦ is genitive as the heard participant, rendered of him; this hearing relation does not add a separate source of preposition.

Actual προσελάβοντο is a middle receiving or taking-to-oneself verb; English splits it as took ... to bracketed them. The subject-related receiver belongs to this middle predicate, without a separately printed Greek them or reflexive pronoun.
Actual genitive article and God noun jointly supply of God; the relation remains with its real nominal head.

18:27.sourceText: βουλομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ διελθεῖν εἰς τὴν Ἀχαΐαν προτρεψάμενοι οἱ ἀδελφοὶ ἔγραψαν τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἀποδέξασθαι αὐτόν· ὃς παραγενόμενος συνεβάλετο πολὺ τοῖς πεπιστευκόσιν διὰ τῆς χάριτος·
18:27.targetText: and he resolving to go through into Achaia, the brothers wrote to the disciples, having exhorted them to receive him, who having come, helped them much who have believed through grace,

groups.note: Actual αὐτοῦ is the genitive subject of resolving in the genitive absolute; English recasts the same participant as nominative he. The actual genitive form is retained.

The one actual dative disciples noun names the written-request recipients and the receiving participants in the immediate infinitive clause. English resumes those people as them in its exhort-to-receive control construction. This is an English role recast: no additional Greek personal pronoun or explicit exhortation object is printed, and the object or attachment of the exhorting participle is not settled by this link.

Actual συνεβάλετο is the aorist middle helping sense of συμβάλλω, rendered helped. This is distinct from its active meeting or conversing use in Acts 17:18. Primary dictionary: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/symballo .

Actual dative article substantivizes the perfect believing participle, the people who have believed. English splits that participant expression as them ... who around much; the actual article remains one identity.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with Achaia and grace have no separate English counterparts.

18:28.sourceText: εὐτόνως γὰρ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις διακατηλέγχετο δημοσίᾳ ἐπιδεικνὺς διὰ τῶν γραφῶν εἶναι τὸν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν.
18:28.targetText: for he was powerfully refuting the Jews publicly, showing through the Writings Jesus to be the Christ.

groups.note: Actual δημοσίᾳ is recorded A-DSF in both analyses and used adverbially, rendered publicly. Its recorded dative adjective form is retained, not replaced by a source ADV tag.
